description: The durable-queue retention rules shared by the TypeScript and Python SDKs. Each case is one HTTP answer to one delivery attempt of ONE queued event; a runner records/enqueues the event, answers the attempt with exactly this response, and checks whether the event is still in the store. Both SDKs run every case; the file is copied byte-for-byte between them.

fields.kind: 'outcome': ur.outcomes.record on a request target (POST /v1/requests/{id}/outcomes; a 2xx body is one bare OutcomeResult). 'artifact-outcome': ur.outcomes.record on an artifact target (POST /v1/artifacts/{id}/outcomes; a 2xx body is { data: [OutcomeResult] }). 'reviewer': ur.reviewer.record of one event whose event_id is reviewer_event_id, then flush() (POST /v1/flywheel/reviewer/events; a 2xx body is { data: [ReviewerEventResult] }).
fields.status: The HTTP status of the answer.
fields.content_type: The Content-Type header of the answer.
fields.body: The response body, exactly as sent (a UTF-8 string; may be empty).
fields.unreadable: When true, reading the body fails (the stream errors after the headers) instead of yielding body.
fields.expect: 'retain': the event is still in the store afterwards (queued or dead-lettered). 'drop': it was removed (delivered, or definitively refused).
fields.outcome: The finer result. Outcome kinds: the receipt status, 'delivered' | 'rejected' | 'queued'. Reviewer: 'accepted' | 'duplicate' | 'dropped' (flush report counters), 'dead_lettered' (kept as a dead letter), or 'pending' (still queued; a non-2xx answer may also raise).

rules.outcome_drop: An outcome event is dropped only on (a) a 2xx answer whose result (the bare body, or data[0] for an artifact target) is an object with status in accepted | duplicate | conflict | rejected (delivered), or (b) a definitive refusal: a 4xx other than 401/403/408/429, whose body is {"error": {code, message, request_id, retryable[, provider_code]}} with code a non-empty string, message and request_id strings, retryable the boolean false and provider_code (when present) a string, and whose code is invalid_request at 400, not_found at 404 or conflict at 409. Everything else retains.
rules.reviewer_drop: A reviewer event is removed only by a 2xx answer {"data": [...]} holding a verdict object with its event_id and either status accepted | duplicate, or status rejected | unsupported with a string reason and repairable false. rejected | unsupported with a string reason and repairable true keeps it as a dead letter. A failed delivery never removes an event.
